subject: [PATCH v2 0/1] mm, swap: only prefer nonfull clusters on synchronous devices

reviews.author: Nhat Pham
reviews.summary:
Reviewer noted that the patch only prefers nonfull clusters on synchronous devices, but did not provide a clear justification for this decision and requested more information about why other types of devices are excluded.

Reviewer Nhat Pham suggested considering also preferring non-full clusters for zswap devices, noting it would require a best-effort check of the folio's cgroup's zswappability.
reviews.raw_body:
LGTM for the most part:

Reviewed-by: Nhat Pham <nphamcs@gmail.com>

Quick comment below:

---

Side note - I wonder if it's worth it to also prefer non-full clusters
for zswap as well?

It's a bit tricky, but I suppose you can do a best-effort check of the
folio's cgroup's zswappability?

2026-11-05.patch_summary: This patch addresses a performance regression in the Linux kernel, specifically related to swap I/O operations on synchronous devices like NVMe partitions. The issue arises from two commits: one that prefers non-full clusters over free ones and another that frees swap slots on exclusive write faults. This leads to scattered writes and increased read requests, resulting in decreased throughput. The patch proposes a solution by only preferring non-full clusters on synchronous devices, which improves performance metrics such as device read and write requests per transaction and throughput.

reviews.author: Kairui Song
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Kairui Song questioned whether only checking for synchronous devices is sufficient and suggested an alternative condition using !si->flags & SWP_SYNCHRONOUS_IO, while still considering the original two checks to be reasonable.

Reviewer noted that the patch is mostly good but suggested keeping nonfull-first only on synchronous devices like zram, which don't merge I/O and where filling holes first keeps the free clusters for large folios.
reviews.raw_body:
I actually wonder if we just want !si->flags & SWP_SYNCHRONOUS_IO
here, but still reasonable to keep the two checks here.

---

That's a pretty nice helper, thanks!

The patch itself looks good to me.

Acked-by: Kairui Song <kasong@tencent.com>

reviews.author: Alexandre Ghiti
reviews.summary:
Reviewer noted that the patch only prefers nonfull clusters on synchronous devices like zram, but this may not be sufficient to address the issue of scattered I/O requests, and suggested reverting commit 3cedb745d354 as an alternative solution.

Reviewer Alexandre Ghiti suggested the patch should be sent to stable since it was merged in 7.3 and added a Reviewed-by tag.

Reviewer noted that the patch's behavior of preferring nonfull clusters on synchronous devices may not be sufficient, as it does not address the issue of holes in full clusters being filled by reclaim, leading to scattered writes and increased I/O requests.

reviews.author: Andrew Morton
reviews.summary: Andrew Morton requested that the patch series be presented as a unified singleton instead of multiple patches.
reviews.raw_body:
Thanks all.

Please avoid single-patch patch series?  Present them as a unified
singleton.

Here's what I ended up with.  Please check.


From: Alexandre Ghiti <alex@ghiti.fr>
Subject: mm, swap: only prefer nonfull clusters on synchronous devices
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 15:18:32 -0800

Commit 9a42aed48421 ("mm, swap: prefer nonfull over free clusters") made
the allocator fill nonfull clusters before taking free ones on swap
devices without discard.  Commit 3cedb745d354 ("mm: clarify the
folio_free_swap() for do_swap_page()") frees the swap slot on an exclusive
write fault.  Such faults now leave holes in formerly full clusters,
putting those clusters back on the nonfull list.  Reclaim allocates slots
one folio at a time, scattering a batch across the holes instead of
producing mergeable writes.  Later swapin can also require more read
requests.

On a mysql/sysbench workload in a 256 MiB memcg swapping to an NVMe
partition, 7.3 compared with the previous version produced 59% more device
read requests and 27% more write requests per transaction.  Throughput was
unchanged without iocost and fell 19% with iocost.

Prefer free clusters first on nonsynchronous devices, preserving
contiguous swap slots for merging I/O.  Keep nonfull-first on synchronous
devices such as zram: they do not merge I/O, and filling holes saves free
clusters for large folios.  Keep free-cluster preference on discard
devices to spread writes.

In the same workload, v2 reduced read requests per transaction by 14% and
write requests by 48% against its base kernel.  Throughput was unchanged
without iocost and improved 33% with iocost.  The RFC's batch-aware
allocator also improved this workload, but this policy needs no batch
information from reclaim.  Reverting the slot-freeing change would keep
swap space pinned under dirty pages; a proposed 50% swap-usage cutoff for
free-cluster preference was arbitrary and would stop helping as swap
filled.

The 7.0 to 7.2 kernels retained the swap slot after a write fault as a
side effect of 4b34f1d82c65 ("mm, swap: free the swap cache after folio is
mapped").  The observed regression requires both 9a42aed48421 and
3cedb745d354; stable backports should target trees containing both.

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20261105155032.240457-1-alex@ghiti.fr
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20261105155032.240457-2-alex@ghiti.fr
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20261022145615.2184343-1-alex@ghiti.fr
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/CAMgjq7BFbXEKEt9faj_rg5AStfLkpJ0j57EQOOJ+L3-w2xRvtg@mail.gmail.com
Fixes: 9a42aed48421 ("mm, swap: prefer nonfull over free clusters")
Signed-off-by: Alexandre Ghiti <alex@ghiti.fr>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>
Suggested-by: Kairui Song <kasong@tencent.com>
Acked-by: Kairui Song <kasong@tencent.com>
Reviewed-by: Nhat Pham <nphamcs@gmail.com>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
---

 mm/swapfile.c |   19 +++++++++++++------
 1 file changed, 13 insertions(+), 6 deletions(-)

--- a/mm/swapfile.c~mm-swap-only-prefer-nonfull-clusters-on-synchronous-devices
+++ a/mm/swapfile.c
@@ -973,6 +973,17 @@ static bool __swap_cluster_alloc_entries
 	return true;
 }
 
+/*
+ * Prefer a new cluster over a nonfull one if the device needs discard, to
+ * spread out the writes, or if it is not synchronous, to keep the slots
+ * of a swapout batch contiguous so that its writes can be merged.
+ */
+static bool swap_prefer_free_cluster(struct swap_info_struct *si)
+{
+	return (si->flags & SWP_PAGE_DISCARD) ||
+	       !(si->flags & SWP_SYNCHRONOUS_IO);
+}
+
 /* Try use a new cluster for current CPU and allocate from it. */
 static unsigned int alloc_swap_scan_cluster(struct swap_info_struct *si,
 					    struct swap_cluster_info *ci,
@@ -1143,11 +1154,7 @@ static unsigned long cluster_alloc_swap_
 	}
 
 new_cluster:
-	/*
-	 * If the device need discard, prefer new cluster over nonfull
-	 * to spread out the writes.
-	 */
-	if (si->flags & SWP_PAGE_DISCARD) {
+	if (swap_prefer_free_cluster(si)) {
 		found = alloc_swap_scan_list(si, &si->free_clusters, folio, false);
 		if (found)
 			goto done;
@@ -1159,7 +1166,7 @@ new_cluster:
 			goto done;
 	}
 
-	if (!(si->flags & SWP_PAGE_DISCARD)) {
+	if (!swap_prefer_free_cluster(si)) {
 		found = alloc_swap_scan_list(si, &si->free_clusters, folio, false);
 		if (found)
 			goto done;
_
